text: Brentano's thesis holds that intentionality — the 'aboutness' or directedness of mental states toward objects — is the mark of the mental, distinguishing mental phenomena from physical phenomena.
explanation: This is precisely Brentano's claim in Psychology from an Empirical Standpoint (1874): every mental phenomenon exhibits directedness toward a content or object, whereas physical phenomena are not about anything. A striking feature is intentional inexistence — the intentional object (Pegasus, a feared monster) need not exist for the state to be directed at it.
